title: Ranveer Singh Dances Garba With Nita Ambani at Swadesh's Navratri Eve Gala
excerpt: The Ambani family hosted a star-studded 'Devi Shakti' night at the Eros Cinema flagship to mark Swadesh's first anniversary on the eve of Navratri.
body:
• On Saturday, 10 October, Nita Ambani hosted a "Devi Shakti" celebration at Swadesh Eros in Churchgate, Mumbai, marking the first anniversary of the Reliance Foundation's flagship art-and-craft store — on the eve of Navratri.
  • Ranveer Singh made a rare public appearance — his first since the birth of his second daughter on 19 September — and a video of him dancing garba with Nita Ambani went viral. Isha Ambani joined the family on the dance floor.
  • The guest list read like a festival fashion roll call: Aamir Khan, Kriti Sanon, Sanjay Dutt, Rashmika Mandanna, Aditi Rao Hydari, Jacqueline Fernandez, Jackie Shroff, Sara Ali Khan, Shanaya Kapoor, designer Manish Malhotra, Gauri Khan and Farah Khan — alongside Mukesh Ambani, Akash and Shloka, Anant and Radhika.
  • Swadesh is Nita Ambani's Reliance Foundation initiative promoting India's traditional arts, crafts and artisans — so the night's real subject was handloom and heritage, dressed up in Bollywood's finest festive wear.

A new dad steals the dance floor on Navratri eve

The biggest talking point of Mumbai's most glittering Navratri-eve party was not the guest list, long as it was. It was Ranveer Singh — new father of two, lately keeping a deliberately low profile — back in his high-energy element, dancing garba with host Nita Ambani in a bright rani-pink kurta, a floral-embroidered jacket, white bottoms, tinted sunglasses and his signature diamond studs.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=4C5vbT3E4A4

The occasion was the first anniversary of Swadesh at the Eros Cinema building in Churchgate, hosted by Nita Ambani on Saturday, 10 October. The evening, themed "Devi Shakti" to welcome the nine-day Navratri festival, drew one of the season's most star-studded gatherings. Footage of Ranveer mid-garba circulated online within hours — a fitting precursor, since Navratri commenced on Sunday, 11 October, and runs through Dussehra on 20 October.

"The evening, themed "Devi Shakti" to welcome the nine-day Navratri festival, drew one of the season's most star-studded gatherings."

The appearance carried personal resonance. On 19 September, Ranveer and Deepika Padukone announced the birth of their second daughter — "Welcome Baby Girl! 19/9/2026. Dua, Deepika and Ranveer" — alongside a tiny footprint. Their first daughter, Dua, was born in September 2024. Since the second baby's arrival, Ranveer has stayed away from events to spend time with family. For fans, seeing the self-described girl dad back on a dance floor was the evening's emotional beat.

Context & Background

To understand the venue, look past the celebrities. Swadesh is the Reliance Foundation's flagship art-and-craft store, founded by Nita Ambani to promote India's traditional arts, crafts and the artisans who keep them alive. Its home is no ordinary retail space: the Eros Cinema building in Churchgate is one of Mumbai's art-deco landmarks, restored into a flagship for handloom and heritage. The anniversary celebration was, at its core, a showcase for India's craft economy — the Bollywood turnout was the amplifier.

https://x.com/Nandini808/status/2109517115669741944

Navratri-eve events have become a fixed fixture of Mumbai's festive calendar, and the Ambani family has made a habit of hosting them at scale. The formula is consistent: a cultural theme (this year, Devi Shakti, honouring the feminine divine and the artisan traditions around it), a dress code that turns the red carpet into a festive-fashion preview, and a guest list that guarantees the evening trends by morning.

Impact & Analysis

Strip away the glamour and the evening did real cultural work. Swadesh's pitch — that India's handloom and craft traditions deserve flagship retail and national attention — gets its biggest annual advertisement on nights like this, when handwoven silk sarees and mirror-work lehengas are worn by the country's most photographed women. Aditi Rao Hydari's classic handwoven silk saree and Kriti Sanon's heavily embellished royal-blue lehenga with silver mirror work were not just fashion choices; they were the products Swadesh exists to sell, modelled on the country's most visible runway.

For Ranveer, the night doubled as a soft relaunch of his public profile. He has kept a quieter profile since the box-office run of Dhurandhar and the arrival of his second child, and he is reportedly attached to upcoming projects including Pralay. A joyful, family-friendly garba video — dancing with one of India's most respected philanthropists, in traditional wear, on the eve of a beloved festival — is about as carefully calibrated a re-entry as Bollywood stages.

What's Next

Navratri runs through Dussehra on 20 October, and Mumbai's garba calendar is now in full swing — expect more celebrity sightings at dandiya nights across the city in the coming days. For the Ambanis, the Swadesh anniversary sets the tone for a festive season in which the family's cultural initiatives tend to take centre stage. And for Ranveer watchers, the question is whether the Swadesh appearance marks the start of a busier public run as his next projects move toward release. The footage from the evening suggests he is ready.
